issue_context.title: Cannot bind configuration to a value type
comments: Oh, and I also can't use `Bind`, since the parameter isn't passed by reference.
I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this issue. Please help me learn by adding exactly one [area label](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md).

Looks like ConfigurationBinder.CreateInstance is missing a special case for structs:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/bd6cbe3642f51d70839912a6a666e5de747ad581/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Binder/src/ConfigurationBinder.cs#L370-L374

It may be that this only requires special handling for the struct case, just checking its public.

@thomaslevesque would you be interested in making a PR to fix this?
@ericstj sure, I'll take a look at it.

review_comments: Do we need to disallow internal value types that a caller wouldn't normally have access to?  We probably don't need to be any more restrictive than we are for classes, but I wasn't sure what was allowed for classes.
Looks like this code already allows creation of an internal type in another assembly if that type had a public constructor, so it looks like this doesn't make that any worse.
